sections.h2: How many days of notice before an Ohio eviction?
sections.html:
At least three in most cases. R.C. 1923.04 requires the party seeking possession to tell the other side to leave three or more days before the court action starts. Delivery can be by certified mail with return receipt requested, by handing a written copy to the defendant in person, or by leaving it at the defendant's usual place of abode or at the premises.

When a landlord is recovering a residence, the notice must carry this statement in a conspicuous place: "You are being asked to leave the premises. If you do not leave, an eviction action may be initiated against you. If you are in doubt regarding your legal rights and obligations as a tenant, it is recommended that you seek legal assistance." Whether a notice includes it is the first thing an owner or buyer should check.

sections.h2: Notice periods that end a tenancy
sections.html:
The three-day notice opens the door to court, but other chapters of the Revised Code set the notice that ends the tenancy to begin with. The table covers the ones that come up most when a rented house is being sold.

Ohio notice periods for ending a residential tenancy
SituationNotice required
Week-to-week tenancy (R.C. 5321.17(A))At least seven days before the termination date
Month-to-month tenancy (R.C. 5321.17(B))At least thirty days before the periodic rental date
Tenant fails a health and safety duty (R.C. 5321.11)Written notice, ending not less than thirty days after receipt
Drug-related violation tied to the premises (R.C. 5321.17(C))Termination three days after the notice is given
Land installment contract (R.C. 1923.04(B))Notice under R.C. 5313.06 counts as the notice to leave

sections.h2: Notice when the tenant is behind on rent
sections.html:
Under R.C. 1923.02(B), a tenant on an oral tenancy who defaults on rent forfeits the right to occupy, and the landlord can end the tenancy with the three-day notice from R.C. 1923.04. A tenant who stays past the end of the term, or who breaches a written rental agreement, can also be sued once that notice has run.

Record how and when you delivered it. Clerks and judges look at the delivery method, so be ready to show the certified mail receipt, the date of hand delivery, or where a copy was left.

sections.h2: Special cases with their own delivery rules
sections.html:
A few situations carry separate delivery steps. When the person to be removed is a deceased resident of a manufactured home park, R.C. 1923.04(C) calls for leaving the notice at the premises and also mailing it by ordinary mail to the executor or administrator if the probate court has appointed one, and to the resident's spouse and other immediate family members whose names and addresses the park operator knows.

Student tenants of a college or university follow a separate path under R.C. 5321.031, which the eviction chapter points to. An owner with a unit of that type should read that section before serving anything.

sections.h2: What a landlord may not do instead of giving notice
sections.html:
Ohio bars self-help eviction. R.C. 5321.15 forbids a landlord from cutting off utilities or services, locking the tenant out, or threatening an unlawful act to recover possession, except through the court process in Chapters 1923, 5303 and 5321. It also bars seizing a tenant's furnishings or possessions to collect rent without a court order. A landlord who breaks the rule owes the tenant all damages plus reasonable attorney fees.

R.C. 5321.02 adds a retaliation rule. A landlord may not raise rent, cut services, or bring or threaten a possession action because the tenant:

  • complained to a government agency about a building, housing, health or safety code violation that materially affects health and safety;
  • complained to the landlord about a violation of the landlord's duties under R.C. 5321.04;
  • joined other tenants to negotiate collectively over the rental agreement.

A tenant can raise retaliation as a defense to the possession case, recover possession, or end the agreement, and can also recover actual damages and attorney fees. A rent increase that reflects the cost of improvements the landlord installed is allowed.

sections.h2: How a notice affects a sale
sections.html:
The notice decides whether the buyer gets an empty house or one with a tenant in it. An owner who wants a vacant house should serve the right notice for the tenancy type, such as thirty days for a month-to-month tenant, then follow the court steps if the tenant stays. A buyer who is happy to keep the tenant can skip the notice and take over the lease.

Security deposits matter at closing and at move-out. Under R.C. 5321.16, a deposit above fifty dollars or one month's rent, whichever is greater, earns five percent annual interest on the excess if the tenant stays six months or more. At the end of the tenancy, deductions must be itemized in a written notice delivered within thirty days after termination and delivery of possession, and the tenant must supply a forwarding address. A landlord who wrongly withholds owes the withheld amount again as damages plus attorney fees.

  • Pull the lease, ledger and any notices before listing.
  • Tell the title company where the deposit sits.
  • Decide in the contract whether the buyer takes the house vacant or tenant-occupied.

A cash buyer will often take a house with a tenant still in it, or give you time to finish the notice process, because there is no lender requiring vacant possession at closing.

A plain-language timeline for tenants starts with the three-day notice: read the notice for the required sentences, try to settle before a case is filed, and put any agreement in writing. Free legal services are available to some low-income tenants through Right to Counsel programs in Akron, Cleveland, Columbus and Toledo, and through local legal aid offices elsewhere.

Landlords can ask the clerk of the municipal or county court that covers the rental address how to file once the notice period has passed. Clerks explain forms and fees but do not give legal advice. Owners with a complicated tenancy, such as a lease with a purchase option or a mixed-use building, should speak with a landlord attorney before serving anything.

faqs.q: Is a three-day notice in Ohio an eviction?
faqs.a: No. It is the required warning before a case. R.C. 1923.04 says the notice must be given three or more days before the court action begins, and only a court judgment can lead to removal by an officer.

faqs.q: Can an Ohio landlord change the locks or shut off the water to force a tenant out?
faqs.a: No. R.C. 5321.15 forbids terminating utilities or services, excluding the tenant, or threatening unlawful acts to recover possession. The landlord owes damages and attorney fees for a violation.

faqs.q: How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy in Ohio?
faqs.a: At least thirty days before the periodic rental date, under R.C. 5321.17(B). A week-to-week tenancy needs at least seven days before the termination date.

faqs.q: Does the Ohio eviction notice have to say anything specific?
faqs.a: Yes. A residential notice under R.C. 1923.04 must contain the statutory statement that begins 'You are being asked to leave the premises.' It must be printed or written conspicuously.

faqs.q: Can I sell my rented Ohio house while a notice is pending?
faqs.a: Yes, an owner can contract to sell, but the tenant's right to remain follows the notice and court process. Settle in the contract who delivers possession and when, and keep copies of every notice for the buyer.
